bull.t: Record backlog and durable infrastructure demand
bull.b: A record backlog and multiyear utility, grid, generation and technology programs provide substantial revenue visibility. Structural investment in electrification, grid modernization and mission-critical infrastructure should support demand over the next several years.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and improving financial flexibility
bull.b: Strong operating and free cash flow gives Quanta resources to fund growth, acquisitions and debt service. Improved leverage and approximately $2.8 billion of liquidity strengthen resilience and support continued investment in expanding infrastructure capabilities.

bull.t: Self-performance capabilities and broader service platform
bull.b: A large craft-skilled workforce and high self-performance level can improve execution control, customer confidence and project capacity. Recent capability additions also broaden cross-selling opportunities across electric, technology, fabrication and industrial infrastructure.

bear.t: Thin margins and material project execution risk
bear.b: Contracting work carries exposure to labor, equipment, subcontractor and project-cost overruns. Quanta's improving but still modest margins provide limited protection if execution issues, input inflation or unfavorable project mix reduce profitability.

Reported backlog does not eliminate timing risk because some large transmission and generation programs are not fully contracted. Permitting pauses could also delay technology projects, making revenue conversion and resource planning less predictable.

bear.t: Higher debt and acquisition integration obligations
bear.b: Although leverage has improved, higher debt increases fixed financial commitments as Quanta expands through acquisitions. Integrating multiple businesses and meeting earnout obligations could pressure returns or flexibility if acquired operations underperform.
